jemalloc_enable_background_threads.desc: Enable jemalloc background threads. Jemalloc uses background threads to cleanup unused memory pages. Disabling it could lead to performance degradation.

jemalloc_max_background_threads_num.desc: Maximum amount of jemalloc background threads to create, set to 0 to use jemalloc's default value

jemalloc_profiler_sampling_rate.desc: Controls jemalloc's `lg_prof_sample` — the base-2 logarithm of the average interval (in bytes) between allocation samples. The default value of 19 corresponds to 512 KiB. Setting it to a smaller value increases sampling frequency (more overhead, more detail), and a larger value decreases it. Changing this value calls `prof.reset` which resets all accumulated profiling statistics. Requires profiling to be enabled (`MALLOC_CONF=prof:true`).

threadpool_local_fs_reader_pool_size.desc: The number of threads in the thread pool for reading from local filesystem when `local_filesystem_read_method = 'pread_threadpool'`.

threadpool_local_fs_reader_queue_size.desc: The maximum number of jobs that can be scheduled on the thread pool for reading from local filesystem.

threadpool_remote_fs_reader_pool_size.desc: Number of threads in the Thread pool used for reading from remote filesystem when `remote_filesystem_read_method = 'threadpool'`.

threadpool_remote_fs_reader_queue_size.desc: The maximum number of jobs that can be scheduled on the thread pool for reading from remote filesystem.

s3_max_redirects.desc: Max number of S3 redirects hops allowed.

s3_retry_attempts.desc: Setting for Aws::Client::RetryStrategy, Aws::Client does retries itself, 0 means no retries

s3_load_table_anonymously_if_credentials.desc: Controls what happens when a persistent `S3` or `S3Queue` table, a dynamic `disk(type = s3, ...)`, or a `DataLakeCatalog` (Glue, BigLake) database is loaded from existing metadata (server startup or `RESTORE`) and its definition would resolve the server's own (ambient) S3/cloud credentials that are blocked for user queries by `s3_allow_server_credentials_in_user_queries`. When enabled (the default), the object is loaded without those credentials instead of aborting startup: an `S3`/`S3Queue` table or a dynamic S3 disk is built with an anonymous S3 client, and a `DataLakeCatalog` database is left with an unavailable catalog. The server starts, but the object is inaccessible (its requests to…

s3_allow_server_credentials_for_system_t.desc: Allows a dynamic `disk(type = s3, ...)` of a table in the `system` database to use the server's own (ambient) S3 credentials, exempting it from the `s3_allow_server_credentials_in_user_queries` restriction. This is for server-internal infrastructure that ships system tables to S3 with the server's identity (attached by the cloud operator into the `system` database). Unlike the session setting, it is a server-level setting, so the exemption also applies when the table is reloaded from metadata on restart. It is scoped to the `system` database, which ordinary users cannot create tables in, so it does not relax the restriction for user queries.

os_threads_nice_value_merge_mutate.desc: Linux nice value for merge and mutation threads. Lower values mean higher CPU priority. Requires CAP_SYS_NICE capability, otherwise no-op. Possible values: -20 to 19.

os_threads_nice_value_zookeeper_client_s.desc: Linux nice value for send and receive threads in ZooKeeper client. Lower values mean higher CPU priority. Requires CAP_SYS_NICE capability, otherwise no-op. Possible values: -20 to 19.

max_zookeeper_pooled_connections.desc: Maximum number of lazily initialized ZooKeeper sessions per ZooKeeper cluster in the shared pool. A value of `0` disables pooled connections and keeps using a single session.

os_threads_nice_value_distributed_cache_.desc: Linux nice value for the threads of distributed cache TCP handler. Lower values mean higher CPU priority. Requires CAP_SYS_NICE capability, otherwise no-op. Possible values: -20 to 19.

enforce_keeper_component_tracking.desc: If enabled, every ZooKeeper request must have a component name set via `Coordination::setCurrentComponent`. Throws a `LOGICAL_ERROR` exception if the component is missing.

keeper_hosts.desc: Dynamic setting. Contains a set of [Zoo]Keeper hosts ClickHouse can potentially connect to. Doesn't expose information from `<auxiliary_zookeepers>`

allow_experimental_webassembly_udf.desc: Enable experimental support for WebAssembly UDFs

enable_silk_runtime.desc: Enable experimental support for the silk fiber runtime: initialize the silk fiber scheduler at server startup, so that subsystems supporting it can run their jobs on fibers

allow_experimental_executable_udf_driver.desc: Enable experimental support for drivers for executable user-defined functions, declared via `user_defined_executable_function_drivers_config`. A driver turns a user code snippet supplied in `CREATE FUNCTION ... ENGINE = DriverName(...) AS '...'` into a runnable executable UDF.

enable_webterminal.desc: Enable the web terminal interface at the `/webterminal` HTTP endpoint. Provides an interactive `clickhouse-client` session in the browser via WebSocket. When `false`, requests to `/webterminal` return HTTP status `403 Forbidden`.

webterminal_allowed_origins.desc: Comma-separated list of full origins (scheme + host + optional port) allowed to open `/webterminal` WebSocket sessions. When empty, the same-origin policy is enforced strictly (Origin must match the request scheme, host, and port). Set this for deployments behind a TLS-terminating reverse proxy where `request.isSecure()` is `false` even though the browser uses `https`. Example: `https://example.com,https://app.example.com:8443`.

webassembly_udf_engine.desc: The engine used to execute WebAssembly UDFs. The only supported value is 'wasmtime'.

allow_impersonate_user.desc: Enable/disable the IMPERSONATE feature (EXECUTE AS target_user). The setting is deprecated.

allow_experimental_cluster_discovery.desc: Cluster discovery is no longer experimental and is always enabled for clusters with the `discovery` section in `remote_servers`. The setting is deprecated and has no effect. It is kept as a `String` so that any previously accepted value, including an empty tag, is still accepted.

allow_experimental_webterminal.desc: Former (experimental) name of `enable_webterminal`. Still honored for backward compatibility when `enable_webterminal` is not set. The setting is deprecated.

s3_credentials_provider_max_cache_size.desc: The maximum number of S3 credentials providers that can be cached

max_open_files.desc: The maximum number of open files. <Note> We recommend using this option in macOS since the getrlimit() function returns an incorrect value. </Note>

path.desc: The path to the directory containing data. <Note> The trailing slash is mandatory. </Note>

user_files_path.desc: The directory with user files. Used in the table function file(), fileCluster().

dictionaries_lib_path.desc: The directory with shared libraries for the `library` dictionary source. The setting is deprecated: the `library` dictionary source was removed.

user_scripts_path.desc: The directory with user scripts files. Used for Executable user defined functions Executable User Defined Functions.

dynamic_user_defined_executable_function.desc: The directory used to keep configuration files of executable UDFs created dynamically by drivers (see `CREATE FUNCTION ... ENGINE = DriverName(...)`). On server restart, the directory is scanned for configuration files and the corresponding UDFs are loaded without invoking the driver again.

top_level_domains_path.desc: The directory with top level domains.

interserver_tables_status_require_auth.desc: Require interserver `TablesStatusRequest` to be authenticated with the cluster `<secret>`. Clients new enough to send a secret hash (protocol revision `DBMS_MIN_REVISION_WITH_INTERSERVER_SECRET_TABLES_STATUS`) are always validated; this setting additionally rejects older clients that send no hash, which is what closes the unauthenticated table-status disclosure by default. Defaults to `true` (secure by default). During a rolling upgrade a not-yet-upgraded node speaks the old protocol and sends no hash, so a `Distributed` query initiated on such a node against an already-upgraded node would have its `TablesStatusRequest` rejected. If you must run a mixed-version cluster, set this to `false`…

interserver_http_host.desc: The hostname that can be used by other servers to access this server. If omitted, it is defined in the same way as the `<hostname -f>` command. Useful for breaking away from a specific network interface.

interserver_http_port.desc: Port for exchanging data between ClickHouse servers.

interserver_https_host.desc: Similar to `<interserver_http_host>`, except that this hostname can be used by other servers to access this server over `<HTTPS>`.

interserver_https_port.desc: Port for exchanging data between ClickHouse servers over `<HTTPS>`.

include_from.desc: The path to the file with substitutions. Both XML and YAML formats are supported. For more information, see the section Configuration files. Empty by default, which means that no substitutions file is used. Before version 26.8 the file `/etc/metrika.xml` was used implicitly whenever it existed; if you rely on it, specify the path explicitly. Note that configuration files that are loaded separately from the main server configuration — the users' configuration (e.g. `users.xml` when it is not included in the main file) and XML dictionary configurations — read the `include_from` element from their own contents, not from the server configuration. Each such file that relies on substitutions…

tmp_path.desc: Path on the local filesystem to store temporary data for processing large queries. <Note> - Only one option can be used to configure temporary data storage: tmp_path, tmp_policy, temporary_data_in_cache. - The trailing slash is mandatory. </Note>

format_schema_path.desc: The path to the directory with the schemes for the input data, such as schemas for the CapnProto format.

google_protos_path.desc: Defines a directory containing proto files for Protobuf types.

filesystem_caches_path.desc: This setting specifies the cache path.

oom_score.desc: On Linux systems this can control the behavior of OOM killer.

oom_canary_enable.desc: Experimental. Enable the OOM canary: a sacrificial child process that attracts the Linux OOM killer before the main ClickHouse server process, giving the server a chance to shed load. Requires Linux >= 5.3 (for `pidfd_open`); the canary is disabled at startup on older kernels. The OOM response requires cgroup v2 `memory.events.local` OOM-kill evidence and may run global query cancellation, merge cancellation, and `system.crash_log` writes. The canary cannot protect the server when cgroup v2 `memory.oom.group` is enabled for the server's cgroup: the kernel then kills the whole cgroup as one unit, including the server, so the OOM response never runs. A warning is logged at startup in this…

oom_canary_size.desc: Size in bytes of the memory region that the OOM canary child process allocates and touches. Locking the region with `mlock` is best-effort: it requires `CAP_IPC_LOCK` or a sufficient `RLIMIT_MEMLOCK`, and when locking fails the canary logs a warning and the memory remains allocated but may be swapped out. Default is 100 MB (104857600). Larger values make the canary a more attractive OOM target.

oom_canary_relaunch.desc: When true, the OOM canary is automatically relaunched after the canary process dies for any reason other than a permanent setup failure or server shutdown — including OOM kills, other signals, and transient exits — subject to `oom_canary_max_rapid_relaunches` and the backoff settings. The OOM response sequence itself runs only when cgroup v2 `memory.events.local` provides OOM-kill evidence.

oom_canary_max_rapid_relaunches.desc: Maximum number of consecutive rapid OOM canary relaunches before automatic relaunch is disabled to avoid thrashing under sustained memory pressure. The counter and the relaunch backoff reset once a canary survives longer than `oom_canary_max_backoff_seconds`, so a canary that dies only sporadically over a long uptime is not eventually disabled. Applies only when `oom_canary_relaunch` is true.

oom_canary_initial_backoff_seconds.desc: Initial backoff delay in seconds between consecutive OOM canary relaunches. The delay doubles on each relaunch up to `oom_canary_max_backoff_seconds`.

oom_canary_max_backoff_seconds.desc: Maximum backoff delay in seconds between consecutive OOM canary relaunches.

remap_executable.desc: Setting to reallocate memory for machine code ("text") using huge pages. <Note> This feature is highly experimental. </Note>

mlock_executable.desc: Perform `<mlockall>` after startup to lower first queries latency and to prevent clickhouse executable from being paged out under high IO load. <Note> Enabling this option is recommended but will lead to increased startup time for up to a few seconds. Keep in mind that this setting would not work without "CAP_IPC_LOCK" capability. </Note>

mlock_executable_min_total_memory_amount.desc: The minimum memory threshold for performing `<mlockall>`

seccomp.desc: What the Linux kernel does when the server makes a system call that it is not supposed to make. At startup the server installs a `seccomp` filter on itself, allowing only the system calls ClickHouse uses. An attacker who manages to run code inside the server process is then left without the kernel interfaces that turn code execution into something worse: loading kernel modules, rebooting, mounting filesystems, `chroot`, changing the process identity, creating namespaces, `ptrace` and reading another process's memory, eBPF, the kernel keyring, `userfaultfd` and `vmsplice`, file handles, `fanotify`, swap and quota control, setting the system clock or the host name, and System V and POSIX…

listen_backlog.desc: Backlog (queue size of pending connections) of the listen socket. The default value of `<4096>` is the same as that of linux 5.4+). Usually this value does not need to be changed, since: - The default value is large enough, - For accepting client's connections server has separate thread. So even if you have `<TcpExtListenOverflows>` (from `<nstat>`) non-zero and this counter grows for ClickHouse server it does not mean that this value needs to be increased, since: - Usually if `<4096>` is not enough it shows some internal ClickHouse scaling issue, so it is better to report an issue. - It does not mean that the server can handle more connections later (and even if it could, by that moment…

listen_reuse_port.desc: Allow multiple servers to listen on the same address:port. Requests will be routed to a random server by the operating system. Enabling this setting is not recommended.

listen_try.desc: The server will not exit if IPv6 or IPv4 networks are unavailable while trying to listen.

mysql_require_secure_transport.desc: If set to true, secure communication is required with clients over mysql_port. Connection with option `<--ssl-mode=none>` will be refused. Use it with OpenSSL settings.

postgresql_require_secure_transport.desc: If set to true, secure communication is required with clients over postgresql_port. Connection with option `<sslmode=disable>` will be refused. Use it with OpenSSL settings.

skip_check_for_incorrect_settings.desc: If set to true, server settings will not be checked for correctness. It also disables the check of the definitions of disks in `storage_configuration`, where an element that no disk of this type reads is reported as `UNKNOWN_ELEMENT_IN_CONFIG` instead of being ignored.

named_collections_storage_type.desc: The storage type for named collections. Possible values are `local`, `local_encrypted`, `keeper`, `keeper_encrypted`, `zookeeper`, and `zookeeper_encrypted`. Configured as `named_collections_storage.type` (`<named_collections_storage><type>` in XML).

query_cache_max_size_in_bytes.desc: The maximum cache size in bytes. 0 means the query cache is disabled.

query_cache_max_entries.desc: The maximum number of SELECT query results stored in the cache.

query_cache_max_entry_size_in_bytes.desc: The maximum size in bytes SELECT query results may have to be saved in the cache.

query_cache_max_entry_size_in_rows.desc: The maximum number of rows SELECT query results may have to be saved in the cache.

logger_level.desc: Log level. Acceptable values: `<none>` (turn logging off), `<fatal>`, `<critical>`, `<error>`, `<warning>`, `<notice>`, `<information>`, `<debug>`, `<trace>`, `<test>`.

logger_log.desc: The path to the log file.

logger_errorlog.desc: The path to the error log file.

logger_size.desc: Rotation policy: Maximum size of the log files in bytes. Once the log file size exceeds this threshold, it is renamed and archived, and a new log file is created.

logger_rotation.desc: Rotation policy: Controls when log files are rotated. Rotation can be based on size, time, or a combination of both. Examples: 100M, daily, 100M,daily. Once the log file exceeds the specified size or when the specified time interval is reached, it is renamed and archived, and a new log file is created.

logger_count.desc: Rotation policy: How many historical log files ClickHouse are kept at most.

logger_stream_compress.desc: Compress log messages using LZ4. Set to `<1>` or `<true>` to enable.

logger_console.desc: Enable logging to the console. Set to `<1>` or `<true>` to enable. Default is `<1>` if ClickHouse does not run in daemon mode, `<0>` otherwise.

logger_console_log_level.desc: Log level for console output. Defaults to `<level>`.

logger_formatting_type.desc: Log format for console output. Currently, only `<json>` is supported.

logger_use_syslog.desc: Also forward log output to syslog.

logger_syslog_level.desc: Log level for logging to syslog.

logger_async.desc: When `<true>` (default) logging will happen asynchronously (one background thread per output channel). Otherwise it will log inside the thread calling LOG.

logger_async_queue_max_size.desc: When using async logging, the max amount of messages that will be kept in the the queue waiting for flushing. Extra messages will be dropped. Rounded up to the next power of two (e.g. `100000` becomes `131072`).

logger_startup_level.desc: Startup level is used to set the root logger level at server startup. After startup log level is reverted to the `<level>` setting.

logger_shutdown_level.desc: Shutdown level is used to set the root logger level at server Shutdown.

openssl_server_private_key_file.desc: Path to the file with the secret key of the PEM certificate. The file may contain a key and certificate at the same time.

openssl_server_certificate_file.desc: Path to the client/server certificate file in PEM format. You can omit it if `<privateKeyFile>` contains the certificate.

openssl_server_ca_config.desc: Path to the file or directory that contains trusted CA certificates. If this points to a file, it must be in PEM format and can contain several CA certificates. If this points to a directory, it must contain one .pem file per CA certificate. The filenames are looked up by the CA subject name hash value. Details can be found in the man page of SSL_CTX_load_verify_locations. The CA certificates are reloaded without a restart when the file changes or on `SYSTEM RELOAD CONFIG`; new connections are verified against the reloaded certificates.

openssl_server_verification_mode.desc: The method for checking the node's certificates. Details are in the description of the Context class. Possible values: `<none>`, `<relaxed>`, `<strict>`, `<once>`.

openssl_server_verification_depth.desc: The maximum length of the verification chain. Verification will fail if the certificate chain length exceeds the set value.

openssl_server_load_default_ca_file.desc: Determines whether the default CA certificates will be used. ClickHouse looks for them in the file `</etc/ssl/cert.pem>` (resp. the directory `</etc/ssl/certs>`), in the file (resp. directory) specified by the environment variable `<SSL_CERT_FILE>` (resp. `<SSL_CERT_DIR>`), and in other well-known locations of various distributions. If no CA certificates are found on the filesystem, no explicit `caConfig` is configured, and the binary was built with embedded CA certificates (the default, controlled by the `ENABLE_EMBEDDED_CA_CERTIFICATES` build option), the embedded certificates are used instead, so TLS works even in a minimal environment without any files, e.g. in a container built "from…

openssl_server_cipher_suites.desc: Supported TLS 1.3 cipher suites in OpenSSL notation. An empty value leaves the OpenSSL default suites in place. `<cipherList>` only applies to TLS 1.2 and below. Suite names OpenSSL does not recognize are ignored; a value that leaves no recognized suite is an error and the TLS context fails to initialize.

openssl_server_cache_sessions.desc: Enables or disables caching sessions. Must be used in combination with `<sessionIdContext>`. Acceptable values: `<true>`, `<false>`.

openssl_server_session_id_context.desc: A unique set of random characters that the server appends to each generated identifier. The length of the string must not exceed `<SSL_MAX_SSL_SESSION_ID_LENGTH>`. This parameter is always recommended since it helps avoid problems both if the server caches the session and if the client requested caching.

openssl_server_session_cache_size.desc: The maximum number of sessions that the server caches. A value of 0 means unlimited sessions.

openssl_server_session_timeout.desc: Time for caching the session on the server in hours.

openssl_server_extended_verification.desc: If enabled, verify that the certificate CN or SAN matches the peer hostname.

openssl_server_required_tls_v1.desc: Require a TLSv1 connection. Acceptable values: `<true>`, `<false>`.

openssl_server_required_tls_v1_1.desc: Require a TLSv1.1 connection. Acceptable values: `<true>`, `<false>`.

openssl_server_required_tls_v1_2.desc: Require a TLSv1.2 connection. Acceptable values: `<true>`, `<false>`.

openssl_server_fips.desc: Activates OpenSSL FIPS mode. Supported if the library's OpenSSL version supports FIPS.

openssl_server_private_key_passphrase_ha.desc: Class (PrivateKeyPassphraseHandler subclass) that requests the passphrase for accessing the private key. For example: `<<privateKeyPassphraseHandler>>`, `<<name>KeyFileHandler</name>>`, `<<options><password>test</password></options>>`, `<</privateKeyPassphraseHandler>>`

openssl_server_invalid_certificate_handl.desc: Class (a subclass of CertificateHandler) for verifying invalid certificates. For example: `<<invalidCertificateHandler> <name>RejectCertificateHandler</name> </invalidCertificateHandler>>`.

openssl_server_disable_protocols.desc: Protocols that are not allowed to be used.

openssl_client_private_key_file.desc: Path to the file with the secret key of the PEM certificate. The file may contain a key and certificate at the same time.

openssl_client_certificate_file.desc: Path to the client/server certificate file in PEM format. You can omit it if `<privateKeyFile>` contains the certificate.

openssl_client_ca_config.desc: Path to the file or directory that contains trusted CA certificates. If this points to a file, it must be in PEM format and can contain several CA certificates. If this points to a directory, it must contain one .pem file per CA certificate. The filenames are looked up by the CA subject name hash value. Details can be found in the man page of SSL_CTX_load_verify_locations. The CA certificates are reloaded without a restart when the file changes or on `SYSTEM RELOAD CONFIG`; new connections are verified against the reloaded certificates.

openssl_client_verification_mode.desc: The method for checking the node's certificates. Details are in the description of the Context class. Possible values: `<none>`, `<relaxed>`, `<strict>`, `<once>`.

openssl_client_verification_depth.desc: The maximum length of the verification chain. Verification will fail if the certificate chain length exceeds the set value.

openssl_client_load_default_ca_file.desc: Determines whether the default CA certificates will be used. ClickHouse looks for them in the file `</etc/ssl/cert.pem>` (resp. the directory `</etc/ssl/certs>`), in the file (resp. directory) specified by the environment variable `<SSL_CERT_FILE>` (resp. `<SSL_CERT_DIR>`), and in other well-known locations of various distributions. If no CA certificates are found on the filesystem, no explicit `caConfig` is configured, and the binary was built with embedded CA certificates (the default, controlled by the `ENABLE_EMBEDDED_CA_CERTIFICATES` build option), the embedded certificates are used instead, so TLS works even in a minimal environment without any files, e.g. in a container built "from…

openssl_client_cipher_suites.desc: Supported TLS 1.3 cipher suites in OpenSSL notation. An empty value leaves the OpenSSL default suites in place. `<cipherList>` only applies to TLS 1.2 and below. Suite names OpenSSL does not recognize are ignored; a value that leaves no recognized suite is an error and the TLS context fails to initialize.

openssl_client_cache_sessions.desc: Enables or disables caching sessions. Must be used in combination with `<sessionIdContext>`. Acceptable values: `<true>`, `<false>`.

openssl_client_extended_verification.desc: If enabled, verify that the certificate CN or SAN matches the peer hostname.

openssl_client_required_tls_v1.desc: Require a TLSv1 connection. Acceptable values: `<true>`, `<false>`.

openssl_client_required_tls_v1_1.desc: Require a TLSv1.1 connection. Acceptable values: `<true>`, `<false>`.

openssl_client_required_tls_v1_2.desc: Require a TLSv1.2 connection. Acceptable values: `<true>`, `<false>`.

openssl_client_fips.desc: Activates OpenSSL FIPS mode. Supported if the library's OpenSSL version supports FIPS.

openssl_client_private_key_passphrase_ha.desc: Class (PrivateKeyPassphraseHandler subclass) that requests the passphrase for accessing the private key. For example: `<<privateKeyPassphraseHandler>>`, `<<name>KeyFileHandler</name>>`, `<<options><password>test</password></options>>`, `<</privateKeyPassphraseHandler>>`

openssl_client_invalid_certificate_handl.desc: Class (a subclass of CertificateHandler) for verifying invalid certificates. For example: `<<invalidCertificateHandler> <name>RejectCertificateHandler</name> </invalidCertificateHandler>>`.

openssl_client_disable_protocols.desc: Protocols that are not allowed to be used.

distributed_ddl_path.desc: the path in Keeper for the `<task_queue>` for DDL queries

distributed_ddl_replicas_path.desc: the path in Keeper for the `<task_queue>` for replicas

distributed_ddl_profile.desc: the profile used to execute the DDL queries

distributed_ddl_pool_size.desc: how many `<ON CLUSTER>` queries can be run simultaneously

distributed_ddl_max_tasks_in_queue.desc: the maximum number of tasks that can be in the queue.

distributed_ddl_task_max_lifetime.desc: delete node if its age is greater than this value.

distributed_ddl_cleanup_delay_period.desc: cleaning starts after new node event is received if the last cleaning wasn't made sooner than `<cleanup_delay_period>` seconds ago.

startup_scripts_throw_on_error.desc: If set to true, the server will not start if an error occurs during script execution.

hdfs_libhdfs3_conf.desc: Points libhdfs3 to the right location for its config.

config_file.desc: Points to the server config file.

dead_session_check_period_ms.desc: How often leader will check sessions to consider them dead and remove

ttl_gc_period_ms.desc: How often leader scans TTL nodes and enqueues TryRemove for expired nodes

ttl_gc_batch_size.desc: The size of the batch of nodes to be removed by the garbage collector

container_gc_period_ms.desc: How often leader scans container nodes and enqueues TryRemove for childless ones

container_gc_batch_size.desc: The size of the batch of container nodes to be removed by the garbage collector

container_gc_max_never_used_interval_ms.desc: How long an empty container node that never had any children is kept before GC deletes it. 0 = disabled (default, container is kept indefinitely).

election_timeout_lower_bound_ms.desc: Lower bound of election timer (avoid too often leader elections)

election_timeout_upper_bound_ms.desc: Upper bound of election timer (avoid too often leader elections)

leadership_expiry_ms.desc: Duration after which a leader will expire if it fails to receive responses from peers. Set it lower or equal to election_timeout_lower_bound_ms to avoid multiple leaders.

reserved_log_items.desc: How many log items to store (don't remove during compaction)

snapshot_distance.desc: How many log items we have to collect to write new snapshot

auto_forwarding.desc: Allow to forward write requests from followers to leader. Has no effect if use_new_dispatcher = true as the new dispatcher has its own forwarding that's always enabled.

shutdown_timeout.desc: How much time we will wait until RAFT shutdown

session_shutdown_timeout.desc: How much time we will wait until sessions are closed during shutdown

startup_timeout.desc: How much time we will wait until RAFT to start.

sleep_before_leader_change_ms.desc: How much time we will wait before removing leader (so as leader could commit accepted but non-committed commands and they won't be lost -- leader removal is not synchronized with committing)

raft_logs_level.desc: Log internal RAFT logs into main server log level. Valid values: 'trace', 'debug', 'information', 'warning', 'error', 'fatal', 'none'

rotate_log_storage_interval.desc: How many records will be stored in one log storage file

snapshots_to_keep.desc: How many compressed snapshots to keep on disk

stale_log_gap.desc: When node became stale and should receive snapshots from leader

max_request_queue_size.desc: Maximum number of request that can be in queue for processing

max_requests_batch_size.desc: Max size of batch of requests that can be sent to RAFT

max_requests_batch_bytes_size.desc: Max size in bytes of batch of requests that can be sent to RAFT

max_read_batch_size.desc: Max size of batch of consecutive read requests that can be executed at once, possibly in parallel

max_read_batch_bytes_size.desc: Max size in bytes of batch of consecutive read requests that can be executed at once, possibly in parallel

parallel_read_threads.desc: Number of threads for parallel local read request processing. 0 means disabled.

parallel_read_chunk_size.desc: Number of read requests each worker picks up atomically when parallel reads are enabled.

parallel_read_min_batch.desc: Minimum batch size to trigger parallel read processing. Smaller batches are processed sequentially.

max_request_size.desc: Max request size (in bytes). Zero means unlimited.

max_requests_append_size.desc: Max size of batch of requests that can be sent to replica in append request

max_requests_append_bytes_size.desc: Max size in bytes of batch of requests that can be sent to replica in append request

max_flush_batch_size.desc: Max size of batch of requests that can be flushed together

min_time_between_fsyncs_ms.desc: Min time between changelog flushes (fsyncs if force_sync is enabled), counted from the start of the previous flush. Flush requests that arrive earlier are delayed to batch more appends into one flush

quorum_reads.desc: Execute read requests as writes through whole RAFT consensus with similar speed

force_sync.desc: Call fsync on each change in RAFT changelog

compress_logs.desc: Write compressed coordination logs in ZSTD format

compress_snapshots_with_zstd_format.desc: Write compressed snapshots in ZSTD format (instead of custom LZ4)

snapshot_zstd_compression_level.desc: ZSTD compression level for snapshots. Lower levels use less CPU but produce larger snapshots. Used only when compress_snapshots_with_zstd_format is enabled.

configuration_change_tries_count.desc: How many times we will try to apply configuration change (add/remove server) to the cluster

max_log_file_size.desc: Max size of the Raft log file. If possible, each created log file will preallocate this amount of bytes on disk. Set to 0 to disable the limit

log_file_overallocate_size.desc: If max_log_file_size is not set to 0, this value will be added to it for preallocating bytes on disk. If a log record is larger than this value, it could lead to uncaught out-of-space issues so a larger value is preferred

min_request_size_for_cache.desc: Minimal size of the request to cache the deserialization result. Caching can have negative effect on latency for smaller requests, set to 0 to disable

raft_limits_reconnect_limit.desc: If connection to a peer is silent longer than this limit * (multiplied by heartbeat interval), we re-establish the connection.

raft_limits_response_limit.desc: Total wait time for a response is calculated by multiplying response_limit with heart_beat_interval_ms

async_replication.desc: Enable async replication. All write and read guarantees are preserved while better performance is achieved.

use_lsmt_storage.desc: Use LSM tree storage for nodes. Has about the same performance but lower memory usage.

storage_memory_only.desc: LSMT: keep all data in memory, don't write to files

block_cache_size.desc: LSMT: size of the in-memory cache of blocks read from files, in bytes. 0 means the size is block_cache_size_ratio of the amount of physical memory.

block_cache_size_ratio.desc: LSMT: size of the in-memory cache of blocks read from files, as a fraction of the amount of physical memory. Used only when block_cache_size is 0.

committed_memtable_size.desc: LSMT: rotate the memtable when it exceeds this many bytes.

uncommitted_memtable_size.desc: LSMT: rotate the uncommitted-state memtable when it exceeds this many bytes.

memtable_block_size.desc: LSMT: target size of memtable blocks, in bytes.

file_block_size.desc: LSMT: target size of blocks in files, in bytes.

file_block_group_compressed_size.desc: LSMT: target size of compressed group of blocks that are read together.

sorted_file_uncompressed_size.desc: LSMT: target uncompressed size of a single file within a sorted run, in bytes.

flush_threads.desc: LSMT: number of background threads flushing memtables to files.

merge_threads.desc: LSMT: number of background threads merging files.

min_files_to_merge.desc: LSMT: background merge will merge at least this many sorted runs at once.

max_files_to_merge.desc: LSMT: background merge will merge at most this many sorted runs at once.

max_size_ratio.desc: LSMT: background merge will merge a range of sorted runs if the ratio [bytes in the lowest-numbered selected sorted run] / [bytes in all selected sorted runs] is less than this. Smaller values reduce write amplification, bigger values reduce the number of sorted runs.

unflushed_memtables_soft_limit.desc: LSMT: throttle writes if there are at least this many memtables waiting for flush.

sorted_runs_soft_limit.desc: LSMT: throttle writes if there are at least this many active sorted runs, implying merges are not keeping up or are misconfigured.

write_throttling_min_delay_us.desc: LSMT: when write throttling kicks in, this is the smallest delay added to a write, in microseconds. The delay grows exponentially (by write_throttling_factor) the further background work falls behind, up to write_throttling_max_delay_ms.

write_throttling_max_delay_us.desc: LSMT: the maximum delay added to a write by write throttling, in microseconds.

write_throttling_factor.desc: LSMT: write throttling delay is multiplied by this factor if soft limit is exceeded by 2x. Should be greater than 1. Delay = write_throttling_min_delay_us * pow(write_throttling_factor, value / soft_limit - 1).

latest_logs_cache_size_threshold.desc: Maximum memory held by the in-memory cache of latest log entries, counting the per-entry allocation overhead and not just the entries themselves.

latest_logs_cache_entry_count_threshold.desc: Deprecated, has no effect. Use log_readahead_commit_window_bytes instead.

disk_move_retries_wait_ms.desc: How long to wait between retries after a failure which happened while a file was being moved between disks.

disk_move_retries_during_init.desc: The amount of retries after a failure which happened while a file was being moved between disks during initialization.

log_slow_total_threshold_ms.desc: Requests for which the total latency is larger than this settings will be logged

log_slow_cpu_threshold_ms.desc: Requests for which the CPU (preprocessing and processing) latency is larger than this settings will be logged

log_slow_connection_operation_threshold_.desc: Log message if a certain operation took too long inside a single connection

use_xid_64.desc: Enable 64-bit XID. It is disabled by default because of backward compatibility

check_node_acl_on_remove.desc: When trying to remove a node, check ACLs from both the node itself and the parent node. If disabled, default behaviour will be used where only ACL from the parent node is checked

snapshot_transfer_chunk_size.desc: Chunk size in bytes for snapshot transfer between Keeper nodes. Larger values reduce round-trips but increase per-message memory usage. 0 means disabled: the whole snapshot is sent as a single NuRaft object (compatibility behaviour).

write_snapshot_version.desc: Snapshot format version to write. Increase only after all nodes in the cluster are upgraded to a version that supports the new format

nuraft_test_mode.desc: Nuraft test mode. not enabled for production use

max_in_flight_request_batches.desc: Maximum number of request batches in flight in the new dispatcher pipeline

max_request_queue_bytes_size.desc: Maximum total bytes in the request queue before blocking new requests

max_response_queue_bytes_size.desc: Maximum total bytes across all response queues; the dispatch thread throttles at half this limit

optimize_read_order.desc: Reorder read requests within a batch to group them together for parallel execution, without changing ordering guarantees within each session

dispatch_busy_wait_sleep_us.desc: Dispatch and response threads periodically poll to check for work to do, sleeping between checks if idle (as opposed to waiting on something like a futex). The sleep duration is dispatch_busy_wait_sleep_us if there was recent activity, gradually backing off to dispatch_busy_wait_long_sleep_us when idle. Reducing these settings reduces request latency by about the same amount but increases cpu usage when the server is idle.

stream_suspect_retry_delay_ms.desc: Delay before reconnecting to the leader after a stream breaks while the new stream is suspected to be unhealthy

stream_in_flight_drain_timeout_ms.desc: Maximum time to wait for in-flight requests to drain after a stream break (e.g. leader change) before dropping them

nuraft_use_bg_thread_for_snapshot_io.desc: Use a background thread for NuRaft snapshot IO instead of reading snapshot objects synchronously from Raft worker threads.

nuraft_streaming_mode.desc: Enable NuRaft streaming mode, which allows multiple in-flight AppendEntries requests to followers instead of strict one-by-one pipeline. Increases write throughput, especially in high-latency environments (e.g. cross-zone Kubernetes).

nuraft_max_log_gap_in_stream.desc: Maximum number of in-flight log entries per follower when streaming mode is enabled. Acts as a throttling cap. Only effective when nuraft_streaming_mode is true.

commit_profiler_real_time_period_ns.desc: Period for real clock timer of the query profiler on the Keeper commit thread (in nanoseconds). The profiling results appear in system.trace_log with query_id = 'KeeperCommit'. 0 means disabled.

nuraft_max_bytes_in_flight_in_stream.desc: Maximum bytes of in-flight data per follower when streaming mode is enabled. Acts as a data volume throttle. Only effective when nuraft_streaming_mode is true.

nuraft_max_uncommitted_log_entries.desc: Maximum number of uncommitted NuRaft log entries on the leader before rejecting new client requests. 0 disables the limit.

slow_member_backpressure_no_progress_tim.desc: How long the leader keeps waiting for a replica that makes no progress at all, while the slow member backpressure is switched on with the `bpon` four letter command, before leaving it behind. Progress means an accepted response: log entries taken, or a snapshot object saved, so a replica that is merely slow keeps resetting this and only one that is stuck stops being waited for. The default is five minutes, and it is meant to be that large: a replica applying a large snapshot can be quiet for minutes and is exactly the one worth waiting for, so a timeout in seconds would abandon it just as waiting started to pay off. A replica the leader cannot reach at all is dropped straight away, without…

slow_member_backpressure_max_uncommitted.desc: The value `nuraft_max_uncommitted_log_entries` takes while the slow member backpressure is switched on with the `bpon` four letter command. Holding the commit index back does not stop the leader appending, so without a tighter limit the log runs further ahead and the replica falls further behind instead of catching up. Tightening it makes the leader refuse new requests with a retriable error until the replica closes the gap. 0 leaves the limit unchanged.

nuraft_append_entries_backward_probe_thr.desc: Number of consecutive backward log-match probes after which NuRaft limits append entries payloads to one log entry. 0 disables the throttle.

nuraft_snapshot_sync_ctx_timeout_ms.desc: Timeout for a single snapshot-install round trip to a follower. 0 means derive it from raft_limits_response_limit * heart_beat_interval_ms (~10 s), which is a request-responsiveness budget and is usually far below the time a large snapshot needs to apply, so a follower that installed the snapshot successfully can have its acknowledgement discarded. Also applies to the add-server snapshot path. Size it against the slowest single-object install round trip - read, queue, transfer, save, apply and response delivery - not against apply time alone. Requires a restart.

log_readahead_enabled.desc: Enable per-peer decoded read-ahead for changelog catch-up reads.

log_readahead_window_bytes.desc: Maximum bytes of decoded entries buffered per peer reader. Should be at least as large as a typical append-entries batch.

log_readahead_max_peer_readers.desc: Maximum number of concurrent per-peer read-ahead readers.

log_readahead_eviction_timeout_ms.desc: Idle timeout in milliseconds after which an inactive per-peer reader, or the commit reader, is evicted. Worst case is approximately twice this value due to the scan gate interval.

log_readahead_pool_threads.desc: Number of threads in the dedicated read-ahead thread pool. 0 = derive from max_peer_readers.

log_readahead_serve_wait_timeout_ms.desc: Maximum time in milliseconds to wait for the background fill before falling back to a direct read.

log_readahead_chunk_size.desc: Number of log entries decoded per chunk under file_mutex in the read-ahead fill task. Smaller values improve responsiveness to rewinds at the cost of more lock overhead.

log_readahead_commit_window_bytes.desc: Maximum total size of decoded log entries buffered ahead of the commit thread. This is a prefetch window, not a cache: entries are produced in order by one fill task and popped by the commit thread as it consumes them, so the window only has to cover the gap between the two rates, and a value in the tens of MiB is already hundreds of thousands of entries. 0 disables commit read-ahead (commit reads entries from disk one by one).

log_startup_read_max_streams.desc: Maximum number of changelog files read concurrently during Keeper startup. 0 = automatically use the number of CPU cores. 1 = use the serial (pre-parallel) startup read. Effective parallelism is capped by the number of changelog files that need to be read; consider lowering on seek-bound storage (HDD, IOPS-capped volumes).

log_startup_read_buffer_size.desc: Per-stream read buffer size (bytes) used while reading changelogs at Keeper startup. Must be greater than 0. The buffer is additionally clamped to the file size.
